variables.context: Same single charge-carrier species, homogeneous conducting segment, transverse area, fixed material/lattice rest frame and DC operating state. Positive axis defines both current crossing and the signed axial mean carrier velocity.
variables.definition: Signed electric charge on each carrier of the selected species and charge state.
variables.domain: Finite nonzero signed charge; physically appropriate to the species. Not net transferred charge and not an arbitrary fit parameter.
variables.source_symbol: q, signed as in the source vector equation and Example 9.3 solution

variables.context: Same single charge-carrier species, homogeneous conducting segment, transverse area, fixed material/lattice rest frame and DC operating state. Positive axis defines both current crossing and the signed axial mean carrier velocity.
variables.definition: Constant transverse area normal to the chosen axial transport direction.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive area; same conducting support as n and v_d.

variables.context: Same single charge-carrier species, homogeneous conducting segment, transverse area, fixed material/lattice rest frame and DC operating state. Positive axis defines both current crossing and the signed axial mean carrier velocity.
variables.definition: Signed axial ensemble-mean carrier velocity relative to the material frame, normal to the cross section.
variables.domain: Finite real, including zero, in the continuum nonrelativistic carrier-transport regime; opposite current sign for negative carriers.
variables.source_symbol: v_d: signed component consistent with source vector v_d and Example 9.3

records.title: DC source terminal characteristic with internal resistance

variables.context: Same two-terminal DC source, ordered terminals a,b and fixed operating state; V=potential(a)-potential(b), emf oriented a positive, I positive leaving a toward the external circuit. Parameters fixed over the declared current range.
variables.definition: Oriented source emf with terminal a chosen as its positive reference.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; supplied for the source temperature, chemistry/state of charge and operating condition.

variables.context: Same two-terminal DC source, ordered terminals a,b and fixed operating state; V=potential(a)-potential(b), emf oriented a positive, I positive leaving a toward the external circuit. Parameters fixed over the declared current range.
variables.definition: Signed conventional current delivered out of source terminal a.
variables.domain: Finite real including zero and negative charging current, within the source equivalent-model regime.

variables.context: Same two-terminal DC source, ordered terminals a,b and fixed operating state; V=potential(a)-potential(b), emf oriented a positive, I positive leaving a toward the external circuit. Parameters fixed over the declared current range.
variables.definition: Effective ohmic series internal resistance; zero denotes the ideal-source boundary.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; actual sources require state-specific estimation and range validation.

variables.context: Same two-terminal DC source, ordered terminals a,b and fixed operating state; V=potential(a)-potential(b), emf oriented a positive, I positive leaving a toward the external circuit. Parameters fixed over the declared current range.
variables.definition: Signed potential difference across the external source terminals.
variables.domain: Finite signed voltage; no positive-load constraint is imposed.

records.title: Carrier number density from material content and carrier yield

variables.context: Same homogeneous single-constituent host material and mobile carrier species, bulk volume, phase, composition, temperature and pressure. M is per mole of the same host entities counted by z; z is mean mobile carriers per host entity.
variables.definition: Mean number of mobile carriers of the selected species per specified host atom or entity.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative, including zero; must be independently justified for material/state, not assumed from total electrons or valence.
variables.source_symbol: Introduced z maps to the example carriers-per-atom factor.

variables.context: Same homogeneous single-constituent host material and mobile carrier species, bulk volume, phase, composition, temperature and pressure. M is per mole of the same host entities counted by z; z is mean mobile carriers per host entity.
variables.definition: Host mass per bulk volume in the specified homogeneous phase.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive; excludes an empty volume.
variables.source_symbol: Introduced rho_m maps to source copper mass density.

variables.context: Same homogeneous single-constituent host material and mobile carrier species, bulk volume, phase, composition, temperature and pressure. M is per mole of the same host entities counted by z; z is mean mobile carriers per host entity.
variables.definition: Mass per mole of the same host entities used to define z.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive; composition/isotopic basis specified.
variables.source_symbol: Introduced M maps to source molar mass called atomic mass in g/mol.

variables.context: Same homogeneous single-constituent host material and mobile carrier species, bulk volume, phase, composition, temperature and pressure. M is per mole of the same host entities counted by z; z is mean mobile carriers per host entity.
variables.definition: Mobile carrier count per bulk volume for the specified species.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; n=0 describes absent mobile carriers and does not define their drift velocity.

records.title: Copper resistance temperature coefficient from relative conductivity

variables.context: Same copper specimen at 20 degrees Celsius (293.15 K), conductivity relative to International Annealed Copper Standard at that temperature; resistance coefficient between material points on a freely expanding specimen (constant mass), not fixed-geometry volume resistivity.
variables.definition: Specimen conductivity at 20 degrees Celsius divided by IACS conductivity at the same temperature.
variables.domain: Finite positive within the commercial-copper calibration population; the arsenic-bearing cast extension is limited to 0.30–0.94. No universal upper applicability bound is inferred from the scalar guard.
variables.source_symbol: Introduced f maps to source n: percent conductivity expressed decimally.

variables.context: Same copper specimen at 20 degrees Celsius (293.15 K), conductivity relative to International Annealed Copper Standard at that temperature; resistance coefficient between material points on a freely expanding specimen (constant mass), not fixed-geometry volume resistivity.
variables.definition: Fractional resistance slope per kelvin normalized to specimen resistance at 20 degrees Celsius.
variables.domain: Positive empirical estimate, not a universal material constant or volume-resistivity coefficient.
variables.source_symbol: Introduced alpha20 maps to source 20-degree resistance temperature coefficient.
